column3: The Hebrew uses forms for God arising and His enemies scattering and fleeing that can express wishes; BSB gives present statements.

The Hebrew calls God the judge of widows; BSB says defender.
The Hebrew says a house in the singular; BSB says families.

The Hebrew says this Sinai and describes the heavens dripping without explicitly naming rain; BSB supplies the One on Sinai and rain.
The Hebrew describes shaking out generous rain and establishing the weary inheritance; BSB says sending abundant rain and refreshing the inheritance.

The Hebrew repeats flee and calls them kings of armies; BSB says kings and their armies flee in haste.

The Hebrew says snowing on Zalmon without a separate comparison marker; BSB says it was like snow falling.

The Hebrew specifies twice ten thousand and places Sinai in the sanctuary; BSB says tens of thousands and supplies as He was at Sinai.
The Hebrew repeats captivity through a verb and noun and has man in the singular; BSB says led captives away and from men.
The Hebrew repeats day by day; BSB says daily. The object of bearing is not explicitly named, while BSB supplies our burden.
The Hebrew names deliverances and exits from death; BSB uses singular deliverance and calls the Lord GOD our rescuer.
The Hebrew has head and hairy crown in the singular; BSB uses heads and crowns.
The Hebrew repeats bring back without an expressed object; BSB supplies them and varies retrieve with bring up.
The Hebrew uses crushing by the foot and a singular dog tongue; BSB says the foot may be dipped and has plural tongues.
